meta.name: Consuma Brand Constitution
meta.source: Consuma Public Communication Audit (Adhyayan Gupta, Jul 2026), Sections 5-6
meta.principle: Every piece of public communication is generated from this file and validated against it. The model never decides the standard; it executes it. Any rule change requires a version bump, a source, and a date.

ID-1.rule: Company name in all body copy is 'Consuma'. 'Consuma AI' is permitted only as a first-mention disambiguator in external press. 'Consuma.ai' is a URL, never a name in prose.

ID-2.rule: The one-line descriptor is used verbatim in bios, boilerplate, email signatures and JD intros. No paraphrases.
ID-2.canonical: Consuma is an AI-powered rapid research platform that turns a research brief into a decision-ready consumer insights report in under 30 minutes.

ID-3.rule: Product name is 'Rapid Research Platform' on first mention; 'the platform' thereafter. 'RRP' only after expansion in the same piece. Never 'AI Engine'.

claims_registry.note: These are the ONLY quantitative claims permitted in any channel. Every retired variant found live in the audit is listed as forbidden. A new number requires a source and a date appended to this registry.

CL-5.canonical: 30+ brands, including Godrej, Britannia, Foxtale and Mosaic Wellness
forbidden: 35+ global brands (unsourced as canonical current figure)

CL-6.rule: No quantitative claim outside CL-1..CL-5 may appear in generated content. New claims enter only via a registry update with source and date.

voice.reference: The founder's press voice, systematised: sharp, specific, contrarian, metaphor-led but disciplined.

VX-1.rule: Short declarative sentences. Average sentence length <= 18 words; no sentence over 28 words.

VX-2.rule: Maximum one metaphor or analogy per piece.

VX-3.rule: Specifics over superlatives. Banned lexicon in all channels.

VX-5.rule: No hashtags in any channel except LinkedIn, where a maximum of 2 topic tags is permitted.

VX-6.rule: Punctuation hygiene: no space before punctuation; maximum one exclamation mark per piece (prefer zero); no ellipsis as suspense.

CH-CTA.rule: Exactly two CTAs exist. Primary: 'Book a demo' (cal.com link). Secondary: 'Download the report'. No other CTA string may appear.

CH-LI.rule: Insight-first: open with a specific finding or a sharp market observation, never with the company. 80-150 words. Close with one CTA from CH-CTA. Max 2 hashtags. No emojis.
structure: hook: finding or contrarian observation (1-2 sentences)
bridge: what this means for insights/brand teams

CH-EM.rule: One idea, one CTA, under 120 words in the body. Subject line of 7 words or fewer, no clickbait. Descriptor ID-2 verbatim if the company is introduced.
structure: 1-sentence relevance hook tied to recipient's category
the one idea, with registry claims only

CH-JD.rule: Open with descriptor ID-2 verbatim as the mission line. Responsibilities are outcomes ('own X, ship Y, report Z'), not activities. End with a 'How we work' block. Same voice rules as all channels.
structure: mission line: ID-2 verbatim + one proof sentence from registry

CH-WEB.rule: Credible B2B register. Hero line stays 'Consumer Research in Minutes' pending a separate hero review; all supporting copy uses registry claims only. CTAs per CH-CTA.
